ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.AllEnemies)` (Conflagration.cs:25-28) == cost 1 / ATTACK / RARE / ALL_ENEMIES. `handles_own_routing = True` is faithful for the same reason as Breakthrough's: C#'s OnPlay runs once and the fan-out happens inside the attack command, so the sim must not let the framework call `on_play` once per enemy.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(2m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new RepeatVar(4)` (Conflagration.cs:19-23) == `_damage = 2` and `_hits = 4`, and `base_hits` (cards/base.py:197-200) reports 4 so the observation encoder sees the multi-hit correctly. Powered damage on both sides.

OnPlay.issue: Damage per hit, hit count, target set and the OUTER loop order are all faithful: `DamageCmd.Attack(2).WithHitCount(4).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` (Conflagration.cs:37-40) runs `for (i = 0; i < attackCount; i++)` with the target list re-derived per hit (AttackCommand.cs:538-546), which is what the sim's `for _ in range(self._hits): living = [...]` does. THE PER-HIT FAN-OUT IS NOT. C# passes the WHOLE valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets, ...)` call per hit (AttackCommand.cs:650), and that command computes every target's DamageResult first, then runs the after-damage hooks over all results, and only then calls `await Kill(killedCreatures)` for the whole batch (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409). The sim instead makes a SEPARATE `DamageCmd.deal` call per enemy (conflagration.py:44-46), so each enemy's death -- including `on_death` and any spawn/buff it triggers -- is fully resolved before the next enemy is even damaged. Observable whenever a hit is lethal to more than one enemy or an on-death effect changes what the next enemy takes: e.g. two enemies at 2 HP, hit 3 of Conflagration -- the game applies both 2-damage instances and then kills both, while the sim kills the first and lets its death hooks run before touching the second. DORMANT: no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage or block, and the batched-vs-sequential Kill produces the same end state without one. Live the moment such a monster is ported (an on-death buffer of its teammates, or one whose death spawns a new enemy mid-attack). The batching itself is damage_pipeline seam territory; what is recorded HERE is that this card is the one that hands the pipeline a multi-target list in the game and a single target at a time in the sim.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Repeat.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Conflagration.cs:45) == `self._hits += 1` (4 -> 5). The damage stays 2 per hit when upgraded on both sides -- upgraded values checked.

guards.what: the hit loop stops when no living enemy remains (conflagration.py:41-43)
guards.rationale: C# breaks on `validTargets.Count == 0 && combatState.IsLiveCombat()` (AttackCommand.cs:547-550) == the sim's `if not living ...: return`. Both also bail once the player has died mid-attack (C# via `Attacker.IsDead`, AttackCommand.cs:540-543; the sim via `ctx.player.is_dead`).

guards.what: the enemy list filters `is_gone`, matching C#'s `where c.IsAlive` (AttackCommand.cs:544-546)
guards.rationale: Unlike card/breakthrough, which uses `is_dead` here, Conflagration uses `is_gone` (`is_dead or escaped`, creatures.py:177-179 (re-pinned 2026-08-04, was :44-46; content shifted, unchanged: is_gone = is_dead or escaped)), which is the correct analogue of IsAlive.
